links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 13, Web Scraping
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: webbrowser, requests, web APIs, HTML, Beautiful Soup, Selenium and Playwright.

links.title: urllib.parse — Parse URLs into components
links.why: urlsplit, parse_qs, urlencode, quote and urljoin: how an address is cut up and built.

links.title: urllib.robotparser — Parser for robots.txt
links.why: can_fetch and crawl_delay, the module that reads a site's rules for crawlers.

links.title: webbrowser — Convenient web-browser controller
links.why: webbrowser.open and its siblings, the module showmap.py uses.

links.title: html.parser — Simple HTML and XHTML parser
links.why: The standard-library HTML parser behind this page's offline examples and behind Beautiful Soup's 'html.parser' choice.

links.title: json — JSON encoder and decoder
links.why: json.loads, which turns a web API's answer into lists and dictionaries.

links.title: Requests: Quickstart
links.why: Response objects, status codes, raise_for_status, streaming a download and the timeout parameter.

links.title: Beautiful Soup Documentation
links.why: The parsers, select() and the search methods the chapter's soup objects rest on.

links.title: Selenium: Locator strategies
links.why: The By locators of Table 13-3 and how find_element uses them.

links.title: Selenium Manager
links.why: How Selenium finds or downloads the driver and the browser by itself, which the chapter's manual driver steps predate.

links.title: Playwright for Python: Locators
links.why: get_by_role, get_by_text and locator, and why locators are strict.

links.title: Playwright for Python: Auto-waiting
links.why: The actionability checks and the 30 second pause the chapter describes.

links.title: RFC 9309: Robots Exclusion Protocol
links.why: The standard behind robots.txt, with the wildcard and end-mark rules, and the statement that its rules are not access authorization.

links.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
links.why: The status code classes behind 200, 301, 404 and 429.

links.title: Changelog of Python 3.14
links.why: Release 3.14.5 lists gh-138907, RFC 9309 support in urllib.robotparser, which changes what can_fetch answers for a path with a star.

links.title: National Weather Service API Web Service
links.why: The free forecast API the chapter names, with its User-Agent requirement.

links.title: A Standard for Robot Exclusion (Martijn Koster, 1994)
links.why: The 1994 consensus text of robots.txt, the first of the six stories on this page.

links.title: Selenium History
links.why: How a test runner for a timesheet application in 2004 became a browser driver.

links.title: Announcing Playwright for Python (Microsoft, 30 September 2020)
links.why: The announcement that brought Playwright to Python.

links.title: CSS selectors - CSS | MDN
links.why: The selector syntax that select() and the browser tools of the chapter understand.

links.title: HTTP response status codes - HTTP | MDN
links.why: Every status code with its class, the table behind the first digit rule.

links.title: Geocoding API - OpenWeather
links.why: The service the chapter's weather program asks for coordinates; its key and parameters.

links.title: A Quickstart to Web Testing with Playwright (PyOhio 2022)
links.why: A talk that shows Playwright's locators and auto-waiting in use.
